title: Tariff Clause on the Chronic Look-Back Period Where Planned Maintenance Has Interrupted an Electric Service Agreement Address
content:
**Electric Service Agreement — Tariff Rules and Regulations: the chronic look-back and planned maintenance at the service address.**

1. The chronic look-back is set by the planned maintenance at the address, because interruptions the company schedules itself extend the period over which repeated interruptions are judged.
2. The chronic look-back is the 24 calendar months before the posting when two or more outage records recorded as planned maintenance began at the address in the 12 calendar months before the posting.
3. It is the 18 calendar months before the posting when exactly one such record began in that period.
4. It is the 12 calendar months before the posting when none did.
5. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. The planned-maintenance records are counted over the 12 calendar months before the posting; the outage records counted within the chronic look-back are those that began less than 24, 18 or 12 whole calendar months before the posting date, as clauses 2 to 4 set it.
6. The chronic look-back is the period over which the outage records at the address are counted toward the chronic threshold.

| Planned-maintenance outage records at the address, begun in the 12 calendar months before the posting | Chronic look-back |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 24 calendar months before the posting |
| exactly 1 | 18 calendar months before the posting |
| none | 12 calendar months before the posting |

**Note on clause 5 (hypothetical record).** A record that began 20 whole calendar months before the posting date falls within a 24-month look-back and outside an 18-month or a 12-month look-back. A planned-maintenance record that began 14 whole calendar months before the posting date does not count toward clauses 2 and 3.
